summary_paraphrase: A wordless book. Neo gets a goldfish for her birthday and it turns out to be a genius. When she goes out to play ball with Dad, the fish, left behind, works out a plan and floats away in its bowl under party balloons, over the city to the sea. Birds pop the balloons and the fish drops into the sea, makes friends, is chased by an octopus and hides in a giant clam that shuts on it. Neo, in a diving suit with the cat, prises the clam open; they hug and swim home, where Dad waves from an underwater house.

humor_notes: Visual absurdity: a goldfish doing sums, reading and stargazing, and engineering a balloon flight; the cat's reactions; the cat in a diving helmet; a no-octopus sign at the end.

repetition.description: red balloons: party decoration, then the thought-cloud plan, then the flying machine
repetition.why: a planted object pays off, so the flight is surprising but fair

repetition.description: round vignettes on a blue disc frame the fish's moments across the book
repetition.why: a design motif rather than a story repetition; its effect cannot be judged from the pages

notes: Wordless: all information is in the pictures, including the fish's motive (left out on page 3) and how the plan works (thought cloud on page 4).
Planted objects pay off: balloons on page 1 lift the bowl on page 4; the octopus peeks from rocks before filling the page (8); the sparkling clam at the page edge (9) becomes the trap (10).
The darkest moment is a colour change: page 10 left is dull grey and brown, the only drained page in the book.
Quiet wide spread (5) between two busy ones gives a breath before the fall.
The cat reacts on most spreads where the family appears (question mark, fur on end, hug).

strengths: planted objects make each turn fair (balloons, octopus, clam)
a child rescues the protagonist; the adult only waits at home
the low point and the rescue share one spread, so peril never sits alone over a turn
a full arc (home, away, danger, rescue, home) told without words
weaknesses: the protagonist's cleverness does not solve the climax; it causes the trouble and is not used again
how Neo knew where to dive is not shown
the octopus threat is not resolved, only escaped
wordless: the fish's motive (loneliness or following Neo) is open to reading

anti_patterns.note: at the climax the genius fish is rescued rather than using its wits

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children. Participation scored for wordless retelling and finding creatures on the seabed spread.
child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated

age_suitability.notes: Mild peril (a fall, an octopus chase, being shut in a clam) resolved on the same spread by a child's rescue; the octopus is cartoon-like. The fish flying off alone and a child diving alone are fantasy, not modelled as safe behaviour; not imitable in a direct way.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
